title: When, before, after
theme: Time clauses (when, before, after, until, by the time, as soon as)
goal: Student uses time clauses with correct tense agreement — present simple for future time clauses, past for past narratives, and signals sequence/duration.
connects_to: M12 (Second conditional) — fechamento do bloco B1, abre B2 com hipóteses irreais.
module_chunks: by the time + present (future) or past
I'll call you when I arrive.
Before you leave, please lock the door.
After we eat, we'll go for a walk.
By the time you arrive, dinner will be ready.

units.title: When in time clauses
units.real_life_context: You promise actions for when something specific happens in the future.

grammar.sentence: I'll call you _____ I arrive.
grammar.explanation: After "when" referring to the future, use present simple — never "will". The main clause can have "will" (I'll call), but the "when" clause stays in the present.

grammar.sentence: We'll have dinner when everyone _____ home.
grammar.explanation: "When everyone arrives" — present simple 3rd person ("everyone" is singular). After "when" in future context, always present simple.

grammar.sentence: She'll start cooking _____ she gets home.
grammar.explanation: "When she gets home" — specific future moment. "When + present simple" is the correct form.

grammar.sentence: I'll text you when I _____ to the office.
grammar.explanation: After "when" in a future context, present simple "get". "Will get" would be wrong in this clause.

grammar.sentence: We'll celebrate when she _____ the exam.
grammar.explanation: "When she passes" — 3rd person singular with -s. After "when", always present simple.

grammar.sentence: I'll let you know when I _____ a decision.
grammar.explanation: "When I make a decision" — present simple base form with "I".

grammar.sentence: When they _____ the news, they'll be happy.
grammar.explanation: "When they hear" — plural "they" uses the base form "hear". After "when" in future context, present simple.

grammar.sentence: I'll call you when I will arrive.
grammar.hint: Nunca "will" após "when" em time clause futura
grammar.answer: I'll call you when I arrive.
grammar.explanation: This is the most important rule for time clauses: after "when", "before", "after", "until", "by the time", "as soon as" — ALWAYS present simple, even when talking about the future.

grammar.sentence: She'll start when she will be ready.
grammar.hint: Após "when" em contexto futuro, present simple
grammar.answer: She'll start when she is ready.
grammar.explanation: "When she is ready" — present simple "is". "Will be" would be wrong inside the "when" clause.

grammar.passage: I'll call you when I arrive at the airport. We'll have dinner when everyone gets home. She'll let me know when she finishes the project. By the time you read this, I'll be on the plane.
grammar.question: When will the speaker call?
grammar.answer: when I arrive at the airport
grammar.explanation: The text says "I'll / I will call you when I arrive at the airport" — present simple in the time clause.

listening_speaking.text: I'll call you when I arrive.
We'll have dinner when everyone gets home.
She'll start cooking when she gets home.
I'll text you when I get to the office.
We'll celebrate when she passes the exam.

units.title: Before and after
units.grammar_focus: before / after + present simple (future) or past (past)
units.real_life_context: You sequence actions — what comes first, what comes next.

grammar.sentence: _____ you leave, please lock the door.
grammar.explanation: "Before" marks a prior action. "Before you leave, lock the door" — locking happens before leaving.

grammar.sentence: _____ we eat, we'll go for a walk.
grammar.explanation: "After" marks a later action. "After we eat, walk" — walking happens after eating.

grammar.sentence: Brush your teeth _____ you go to bed.
grammar.explanation: Brushing your teeth happens BEFORE sleeping. "Before you go to bed" — present simple after "before" (routine/future).

grammar.sentence: _____ I get home from work, I usually cook dinner.
grammar.explanation: "After I get home" — describes a daily sequence: arriving home, then cooking. "After + present simple" for routine.

grammar.sentence: I'll text you before I _____ to the meeting.
grammar.explanation: "Before I go" — present simple base form. Time clauses always use present simple, even in future contexts.

grammar.sentence: After she _____ the report, she'll send it to you.
grammar.explanation: "After she finishes" — 3rd person singular with -es. "After + present simple" for future sequence.

grammar.sentence: Before you _____, please clean the kitchen.
grammar.explanation: "Before you leave" — a request for before departure. Present simple base form with "you", never "will".

grammar.sentence: I'll call you before I will arrive.
grammar.hint: Após "before" em contexto futuro, present simple
grammar.answer: I'll call you before I arrive.
grammar.explanation: Same rule as "when": after "before"/"after"/"until" referring to the future, always present simple. Never "will" inside the time clause.

grammar.sentence: After we will eat, we'll watch a movie.
grammar.answer: After we eat, we'll watch a movie.
grammar.explanation: "After we eat" — present simple. "Will" only in the main clause (we'll watch).

grammar.passage: Before you leave, please lock the door. After we eat dinner, we'll go for a walk. I'll text you before I arrive. After she finishes the report, she'll send it.
grammar.question: When will the speaker text?
grammar.explanation: The text says "I'll / I will text you before I arrive" — present simple "arrive" after "before" in future context.

listening_speaking.text: Before you leave, please lock the door.

units.title: Until and by the time
units.grammar_focus: until/till (continuous duration) + by the time (point of completion)
units.real_life_context: You express duration ("until something happens") and points of completion ("by the time something").

grammar.sentence: I'll wait _____ you arrive.
grammar.explanation: "Until" = up to (continuous duration up to a point). "I'll / I will wait until you arrive" — the waiting continues up to that moment.

grammar.sentence: _____ you finish reading, dinner will be ready.
grammar.explanation: "By the time" = when + before (at or before that moment). Here: dinner ready before or exactly when you finish reading.

grammar.sentence: Stay here _____ I get back.
grammar.explanation: "Stay until I get back" — continuous duration. You stay HERE the whole time until I return.

grammar.sentence: _____ we arrive, the movie will have started.
grammar.explanation: "By the time we arrive" — when we arrive, the movie will already have started. Marks a temporal reference point.

grammar.sentence: Don't leave _____ I tell you to.
grammar.explanation: "Until I tell you" — stay here the whole time, until you get permission. Duration.

grammar.sentence: By the time I _____ home, my parents will be asleep.
grammar.explanation: "By the time I get home" — when I get home, they'll already be asleep. Present simple after "by the time" in future contexts.

grammar.sentence: I'll keep trying _____ I succeed.
grammar.explanation: "Until I succeed" — keep trying the whole time until succeeding. Duration.

grammar.sentence: I'll wait until you will arrive.
grammar.explanation: Like "when"/"before"/"after", "until" also doesn't take "will" in the future clause. Present simple "arrive".

grammar.sentence: By the time you will finish, I'll be home.
grammar.answer: By the time you finish, I'll be home.
grammar.explanation: "By the time you finish" — present simple. "Will" only in the main clause "I'll / I will be home".

grammar.passage: I'll wait until you arrive at the station. By the time we finish dinner, it'll be 10pm. Stay here until I get back. By the time I write this, my flight will be boarding.
grammar.question: What will the speaker do until the listener arrives?
grammar.explanation: The text says "I'll / I will wait until you arrive at the station".

units.title: As soon as
units.real_life_context: You express that one action will happen immediately after another.

grammar.sentence: I'll call you _____ I get home.
grammar.explanation: "As soon as" = the exact moment when / right after. Immediate action following another.

grammar.sentence: As soon as she _____ the news, she'll be happy.
grammar.explanation: "As soon as she hears" — present simple 3rd person "hears". After "as soon as" in future contexts, present simple.

grammar.sentence: Send me a message _____ you arrive.
grammar.explanation: "As soon as you arrive" — immediately upon arrival. Immediacy.

grammar.sentence: I'll let you know as soon as I _____ a decision.
grammar.explanation: "As soon as I make a decision" — present simple after "as soon as" in future contexts.

grammar.sentence: As soon as they _____ home, they'll start cooking.
grammar.explanation: "As soon as they get home" — plural without -s. Immediate reaction.

grammar.sentence: Call me as soon as you _____ help.
grammar.explanation: "As soon as you need help" — immediate. A promise of availability, present simple base form.

grammar.sentence: I'll start as soon as the music _____.
grammar.explanation: "As soon as the music begins" — 3rd person singular "begins" with -s.

grammar.sentence: I'll text you as soon as I will arrive.
grammar.answer: I'll text you as soon as I arrive.
grammar.explanation: "As soon as" follows the same rule as the other time clauses: present simple in the future, never "will".

grammar.sentence: As soon as she will hear, she'll call me.
grammar.answer: As soon as she hears, she'll call me.
grammar.explanation: "Hears" — 3rd person present simple. "Will" only in the main clause "she'll / she will call".

grammar.passage: I'll call you as soon as I get home. As soon as she hears the news, she'll be thrilled. Let me know as soon as you arrive. As soon as I have updates, I'll share them.
grammar.question: When will the speaker share updates?
grammar.answer: as soon as I have updates
grammar.explanation: The text says "As soon as I have updates, I'll / I will share them" — present simple "have" after "as soon as".

units.title: All time clauses combined
units.grammar_focus: Integration of when/before/after/until/by the time/as soon as
units.real_life_context: You combine time clauses fluidly in conversation about plans, deadlines, and sequences.

grammar.sentence: I'll call you _____ I arrive at the hotel.
grammar.explanation: "As soon as" para imediato. Outra opção válida seria "when".

grammar.sentence: _____ you leave, please turn off the lights.
grammar.explanation: "Before you leave" — an action prior to departure.

grammar.sentence: I'll wait here _____ you call me back.
grammar.explanation: "Until you call back" — duration of the wait.

grammar.sentence: _____ the meeting ends, I'll have lunch.
grammar.explanation: "After the meeting ends" — sequence: lunch after the meeting.

grammar.sentence: By the time I _____ home, dinner will be ready.
grammar.explanation: "By the time I get home" — future reference point. Present simple after "by the time".

grammar.sentence: Don't leave until I _____ you the documents.
grammar.explanation: "Until I give you" — duration until you receive the documents. Present simple after "until".

grammar.sentence: After we _____ dinner, let's relax.

grammar.answer: I'll text you as soon as I land.
grammar.explanation: "As soon as I land" — present simple. This rule applies to ALL time clauses (when, before, after, until, by the time, as soon as).

grammar.explanation: Present simple "read" after "by the time". "Will" only in the main clause.
